haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes. If not claimed in time, Inventory's timer marks it EXPIRED and returns stock to sale. Order is not told. Claim can still succeed if lines remain free.
haiku-low.q2: Before charging. If any line is short, Inventory reserves nothing and publishes StockShort. Order is rejected, no payment is requested, and the customer is told which items are short.
haiku-low.q3: The order id is sent as the idempotency key, so the provider treats retries as the same request. The provider sees one charge.
haiku-low.q4: Claim fails, so Order is CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and emails the customer a full refund. Payment saves a full-amount refund, refunds it, and Order emails refund issued.
haiku-low.q5: Only when OrderConfirmed is published, and Cart empties it. If checkout fails at any point, the cart is left exactly as it was.
haiku-low.q6: Order service moves checkout between steps via events. Its orders table holds the order status, which records how far each checkout has got.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment. Payment updates the payment and writes a PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined outbox event, which Order consumes.
haiku-low.q8: Payment records the provider event id in its webhook inbox in the same transaction. Repeats are ignored, and webhooks for non-PENDING payments get a 200 with no action.
haiku-low.q9: Payment publishes PaymentDeclined, and Inventory releases the hold on receiving it. Releasing an expired or already released hold does nothing.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory's claim step checks that the hold is still HELD, or lapsed with every line still free. If so it claims and Order fulfils. Otherwise ClaimFailed triggers a refund.
haiku-low.q11: The refund stays REFUND_PENDING and is retried with growing delay using the same key, never dropped. A person is alerted after 5 failures. It is tracked in Payment's refunds table.
haiku-low.q12: The OrderConfirmed event causes the Cart service to empty the cart. No other event or service clears it.

sonnet.q1: Held 10 minutes (expires_at = now + 10 min). After that a timer (every minute) marks it EXPIRED and puts the stock back on sale, without notifying Order. A later claim still succeeds if all lines are still free; otherwise it fails.
sonnet.q2: Reserved before charging. If any line is short, Inventory reserves nothing (all-or-nothing, one transaction), publishes StockShort, Order is REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, the customer is told which items are short, and no payment is requested.
sonnet.q3: The idempotency key (the order id) is sent to the provider on every retry, so the provider treats it as the same request and charges once. Payment's unique order id on the payment row also prevents duplicate rows.
sonnet.q4: Claim fails, Inventory publishes ClaimFailed; Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, emails the customer, and publishes RefundRequested. Payment issues a full refund (REFUND_PENDING then REFUNDED); a refund-issued email follows.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only on OrderConfirmed. If checkout fails (any failure case, including late success), the cart stays exactly as it was.
sonnet.q6: No single orchestrator; steps advance by events on the broker, with Order steering checkout and deciding the final outcome. The record of progress is the order status in Order's own database (PENDING_STOCK, AWAITING_PAYMENT, PAID, CONFIRMED, etc.).
sonnet.q7: The provider calls Payment by webhook. Payment records the result and writes a PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined outbox entry, published as an event on the broker to Order. Order then sets PAID and publishes ClaimStock; Inventory's StockClaimed leads Order to CONFIRMED.
sonnet.q8: Payment's webhook inbox of provider event ids (unique constraint) plus the check that the payment is no longer PENDING; a repeat gets a 200 reply and nothing is done. Consumers also keep inboxes of handled event ids, ignoring repeats.
sonnet.q9: Inventory releases the hold and the stock goes back on sale. It is triggered by the PaymentDeclined event published by Payment. Releasing a hold that is already released or expired does nothing.
sonnet.q10: On PaymentSucceeded, Order publishes ClaimStock and Inventory checks in one transaction whether the hold is still HELD or, if lapsed, whether stock on hand minus other live holds still covers every line. If yes: claim, StockClaimed, fulfil. If any line is short: ClaimFailed, order cancelled and full refund.
sonnet.q11: The refund stays REFUND_PENDING, the attempt is recorded, and it is retried with growing delay and the same idempotency key, never given up. After 5 failures a person is alerted and retries continue. It is tracked in Payment's refunds table (order id unique, amount, status, attempts).
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, published by Order after StockClaimed. The Cart service empties the cart on receiving it.
